issues.t: Lower intake manifold gasket leaks coolant
issues.sym: Coolant keeps dropping, the low coolant light comes on, a sweet smell, coolant drips at the front of the engine, overheating, or milky oil.
issues.why: The lower intake manifold gaskets on these V6 engines break down with age and heat and let coolant escape outside or into the oil. It is the most reported engine problem on the 2000-2003 Impala.
issues.next: Have it repaired soon. Do not keep topping off and driving, because coolant in the oil can ruin the bearings and an overheat can damage the heads.

issues.t: Passlock anti-theft no-start
issues.sym: The engine cranks but will not start, or starts and dies, and the security light flashes. It may start again after sitting.
issues.why: The Passlock sensor in the ignition lock housing can fail, so the car thinks it is being stolen and cuts fuel. Owners report replacing several modules before the real fault is found.
issues.next: Leaving the key in On for about ten minutes may let the system relearn and start. For a lasting fix, have a shop that knows Passlock test the sensor and lock housing before swapping computers.

issues.t: Oil can drip onto the exhaust and catch fire (recalls)
issues.sym: A burning oil smell, smoke from under the hood, or oil wetting the front valve cover and exhaust manifold.
issues.why: Oil from the valve cover area can drop onto the hot exhaust manifold, especially under hard braking, and ignite. GM recalled the cars, then issued an improved fix and told owners to park outside until it was done.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and call 911 if there are flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Run the VIN for recalls 09V-116, 15V-701 and 15V-201. Until the repair is done, park outside and away from buildings, and stop driving if you smell burning oil.

issues.t: Ignition can be bumped out of Run (recall)
issues.sym: The engine shuts off while driving, often after a bump or with a heavy key ring, and steering and braking get much harder.
issues.why: A heavy key ring or a jolt can turn the key out of Run, cutting engine power and possibly keeping the airbags from deploying.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Take everything but the key off the ring and run the VIN for recall 14V-400.

issues.t: Fuel pressure regulator leak can cause a backfire (recall)
issues.sym: A fuel smell, rough running, or a loud backfire from the engine.
issues.why: The fuel pressure regulator could leak fuel into the intake, which can cause a backfire strong enough to crack the intake manifold.
issues.next: Run the VIN for recall 04V-090. If you smell fuel, do not drive until it is checked.

issues.t: Driver airbag inflator may fracture (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no symptom before a crash.
issues.why: The driver airbag inflator could crack at a weld when it deploys.
issues.next: Run the VIN for recall 02V-222 and have the module inspected or replaced.

issues.t: Front brake caliper bolts may be loose (recall)
issues.sym: A clunk or rattle from a front wheel when braking, pulling, or a wheel that drags or locks.
issues.why: Some front caliper bolts were not tightened to spec at the factory. A loose caliper can lock a wheel or tear a brake hose.
issues.next: Run the VIN for recall 04V-287. If you hear a clunk at a front wheel while braking, stop driving and have it checked.

issues.t: 4-speed automatic slips or shifts harshly
issues.sym: A hard bang into gear, slipping when accelerating, a slow or rough shift from reverse to drive, or the transmission stuck in one gear.
issues.why: The 4-speed automatic used through 2011 often develops solenoid, pressure control and internal wear problems. Some cases are electronic and simpler to fix; others need a rebuild.
issues.next: Have the codes and fluid checked at the first sign. Catching it before it slips badly leaves more repair options.

issues.t: Head or intake gasket coolant leak
issues.sym: Coolant level keeps dropping, poor heat from the heater, overheating, rough idle, white exhaust smoke, or milky oil.
issues.why: The V6 engines in this generation can leak coolant at the cylinder head and intake gaskets. GM issued a service bulletin for external coolant leaks from the head gaskets.
issues.next: Have the cooling system pressure tested soon. Stop driving if the temperature gauge climbs, because overheating can warp the heads.

issues.t: Ignition key can turn off while driving (recall)
issues.sym: The engine shuts off unexpectedly, often after a bump with a heavy key ring, and you lose power steering and brake assist.
issues.why: The weight of the key ring or a jolt can pull the ignition out of Run. GM recalled the cars to change the key design. The 2014 Impala Limited is included.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Remove extra items from the key ring and run the VIN for recall 14V-355.

issues.t: Passenger airbag sensor wiring can be damaged (recall)
issues.sym: The airbag warning light comes on, or the passenger airbag shows as off with an adult seated.
issues.why: The front seat frame can rub through the wiring for the passenger presence sensor, which may disable the passenger airbag.
issues.next: Run the VIN for recall 16V-507 and have the wiring repaired.

issues.t: Front seat belt may not be attached properly (recall)
issues.sym: Usually nothing until a crash.
issues.why: On some cars the front belt webbing was not properly attached to the lap belt pretensioner anchor.
issues.next: Run the VIN for recall 10V-480 and have the belts inspected.

issues.t: Power steering hose near the catalytic converter (fire recall)
issues.sym: A burning smell, smoke, or power steering fluid leaking at the front of the engine.
issues.why: The upper power steering hose could be routed too close to the catalytic converter, so leaking fluid could land on it and catch fire.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and call 911 if there are flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Run the VIN for recall 11V-398. Stop driving if you smell burning fluid or see smoke.

issues.t: Electric parking brake may stay partly applied (fire recall)
issues.sym: A hot brake smell, smoke from a rear wheel, or the car feeling like it is dragging after releasing the parking brake.
issues.why: The electric parking brake actuator may not fully retract, leaving the rear pads rubbing. The heat can start a fire. Some cars were also repaired incorrectly the first time.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and call 911 if there are flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Run the VIN for recalls 14V-541, 15V-085 and 15V-202. If a rear wheel smells hot or smokes, stop and do not keep driving.

issues.t: Sudden loss of power steering assist (recall)
issues.sym: Steering suddenly becomes very heavy, often with a power steering warning message.
issues.why: A poor electrical ground connection can cut power to the electric power steering.
issues.next: If the steering suddenly turns heavy, grip the wheel with both hands, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — have it towed and checked. Run the VIN for recall 14V-450. You can still steer, but it takes much more effort, so slow down and have it fixed.

issues.t: Shifter cable can disconnect so the car is not really in Park (recall)
issues.sym: The shifter shows Park but the car can roll, or the shifter feels loose.
issues.why: The shift cable adjuster can come apart, so the transmission may not actually be in Park.
issues.next: Always set the parking brake, and run the VIN for recall 14V-092.

issues.t: Body control module short can stall the car (recall)
issues.sym: Unexpected stalling, warning lights, or electrical features acting up.
issues.why: Contamination in the chassis electronic module could cause a short that shuts the engine off.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Run the VIN for recall 14V-614 and have the module serviced.

issues.t: Airbags left in factory mode will not deploy (recall)
issues.sym: The airbag warning light may stay on.
issues.why: On some cars the airbag sensing module left the factory still set to manufacturing mode, so the airbags would not go off in a crash.
issues.next: Run the VIN for recall 14V-518 and have the module reprogrammed right away.

issues.t: Brake lights flash without braking (recall)
issues.sym: Brake lights flicker or come on without your foot on the pedal, and cruise control may switch off by itself.
issues.why: A brake lamp circuit fault can send false brake signals.
issues.next: Run the VIN for recall 13V-220.

issues.t: Passenger airbag may stay on with a child seat (recall)
issues.sym: The passenger airbag indicator shows ON with a child seat in the front seat.
issues.why: The occupant sensing system may fail to turn off the passenger airbag when a child seat is installed.
issues.next: Put child seats in the back and run the VIN for recall 15V-465.

issues.t: Rear brake caliper pistons may lose braking (recall)
issues.sym: The brake pedal feels soft or the car takes longer to stop.
issues.why: Some rear caliper pistons had a poor coating that can let gas pockets form, cutting rear braking power.
issues.next: Run the VIN for recall 18V-576. If braking feels weak, have it checked before driving further.

issues.t: Police-package front lower control arms can crack (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking or rattling from the front end, loose steering, or uneven front tire wear.
issues.why: On police-duty Impalas the front lower control arms can fracture under heavy use, which can let a front wheel move out of place.
issues.next: If the car was a police car, check the VIN for this recall and have both arms replaced. Stop driving if the front end knocks badly.

issues.t: Fuel tank can let vapor seep through (recall)
issues.sym: A fuel smell around the back of the car, strongest in warm weather or after filling up.
issues.why: Some tanks were built without a sealing layer, so fuel vapor can pass through the plastic.
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall and have the tank inspected and replaced if needed. Do not ignore a fuel smell.

issues.t: Fuel return line can tear in a front crash (recall)
issues.sym: Nothing in normal driving. It matters only after a frontal impact, when fuel can leak.
issues.why: On certain cars without anti-lock brakes the fuel return line could be cut in a front crash, which is a fire risk.
issues.next: Check the VIN and have the bracket kit fitted free if the recall is still open.

issues.t: Center console lid may not stay latched (recall)
issues.sym: The console lid pops open on its own, or the latch feels weak.
issues.why: The storage door latch may not hold, so the lid and whatever is inside can fly open in a crash.
issues.next: Have the latch inspected or replaced free under the recall. Keep heavy items out of the console in the meantime.

issues.t: Driver airbag may not deploy properly (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no sign at all, though an airbag warning light should never be ignored.
issues.why: Some driver airbags may not inflate as designed, and the inflator itself could rupture when it does fire.
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall and have the airbag inspected and replaced free if it is affected.

issues.t: Seat belt buckle bases may not be heat treated (recall)
issues.sym: A buckle that feels weak, sticks, or does not latch with the usual firm click.
issues.why: Buckle bases from certain production dates may not have been hardened properly, so the belt may not hold in a crash.
issues.next: Have the buckle date codes checked under the recall and the buckles replaced free if affected.

issues.t: Electric power steering can quit and leave the wheel heavy
issues.sym: A driver information centre message and a chime warn that power steering is reduced or off, and the wheel suddenly needs far more effort, which is worst when parking or turning slowly.
issues.why: This car uses a belt driven electric power steering unit. A poor ground at the steering control module, a loose high current fuse, or a failure inside the unit itself drops the assist out, either at startup or while you are moving.
issues.next: If the steering suddenly turns heavy, grip the wheel with both hands, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — have it towed and checked. Expect the steering to go heavy with no warning, so get it inspected promptly. Ask the shop to check the steering module ground and fuse and the module software before quoting a whole new steering gear.
